body:
`case_study:unitech-2008` | 2008-01-15 | tickers: UNITECH | confidence: verified

Unitech hit Rs 546.80 on the BSE in Jan 2008 (one of India's most valuable realty stocks), fell >90% to ~Rs 30 by Feb 2009 (one day -51% in Oct 2008), ~Rs 21.7 in 2011, ~Rs 7 by Dec 2017 (~-98.7%). Business Standard: Unitech and RCom wiped ~97% of shareholder wealth in 10 years. Visible flags: (1) 2006-07 debt-funded land purchases at cycle-peak prices; consolidated debt ballooned just as the 2008 credit crunch hit; (2) diversification into telecom (Unitech Wireless, 2008 2G licences) -- capital allocation outside the core; later CBI 2G charges against MD Sanjay Chandra (jailed 2011; brothers jailed again 2017 over homebuyer funds); (3) homebuyer advances (customer money) used to fund other projects -- ~Rs 7,800 cr owed to ~16,300 buyers across 61 projects; (4) repeated QIPs/dilution in 2009 to survive; (5) project delays and rising 'inventory' with little cash conversion. In Jan 2020 the Supreme Court allowed the government to take over the board. Lesson: in real estate, track customer-advance usage, debt/equity and land bought with borrowed money at peak; operating cash flow, not land-bank value, keeps a developer alive.

**Lesson:** Leverage + peak-cycle land = ruin; diversification is a red flag
**Spotted early by:** credit markets in 2008; homebuyers
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:avoid-ruin`, similar_to -> `case_study:capital-goods-2007`
**Sources:** <https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/companies/unitech-the-decline-of-realty-major-117120900053_1.html> ; <https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/markets/2g-scam-unitech-rcom-wipe-out-97-shareholder-wealth-in-10-years-117122100260_1.html> ; <https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/features/story/challenges-for-unitech-builders-18937-2011-04-21>

body:
`insight:india-dividend-buyback-tax` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-09-03

Dividends: since FY2020-21 (Finance Act 2020 abolished DDT) dividends are taxed in shareholders' hands at slab rates (up to ~35.9% with surcharge/cess for top individuals; surcharge on dividends capped at 15%), with TDS of 10% above the annual threshold. Capital gains on listed equity from 23 Jul 2024: LTCG (held >12 months) 12.5% above Rs1.25 lakh annual exemption; STCG 20%. Buybacks (Business Today, Sep-2026): (1) to 30 Sep 2024 - company paid buyback tax u/s 115QA (~23.3% effective), shareholders exempt, making tender buybacks the tax-efficient payout for promoters and HNIs; (2) 1 Oct 2024 to 31 Mar 2026 - whole buyback consideration taxed as deemed dividend u/s 2(22)(f) at slab, cost of shares allowed only as a capital loss (e.g., Rs50 lakh buyback on Rs10 lakh cost = Rs50 lakh dividend income + Rs10 lakh capital loss) - buybacks became tax-inefficient for high-slab holders and volumes fell; (3) from 1 Apr 2026 (Budget 2026 / Income-tax Act 2025) - back to capital gains (consideration minus cost) at 12.5%/20% for non-promoters, with an additional levy making promoters' effective rate ~22% (corporate) / ~30% (non-corporate). Implications: (a) for a high-slab Indian investor, a low-payout compounder that reinvests at high ROCE is more tax-efficient than a high-dividend stock (only 12.5% on eventual LTCG, deferred); (b) dividend yield screens overstate post-tax yield for top-bracket investors by ~1/3; (c) buyback announcements should be judged on price vs value (Buffett 2023) and on the tax regime in force on the record date.

Sources:
- https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/story/buyback-tax-how-india-changed-the-rules-three-times-in-18-months-and-what-investors-need-to-know-553004-2026-09-03
- https://www.business-standard.com/budget/news/budget-2026-buyback-proceeds-to-be-treated-as-capital-gains-126020101050_1.html
- https://freefincal.com/budget-2024-how-share-buybacks-will-be-taxed-from-1st-oct-2024/
- https://caalley.com/news-updates/budget-2026/budget-2026-buy-back-proceeds-will-be-taxed-as-capital-gains-for-shareholders-but-promoters-pay-an-extra-price

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-ISRG:fy2026-procedure-growth-14-5-plus`
- **Method:** promise-tracker credibility · **P(ours)** 0.45 · **P(base)** 0.50 · resolve by 2027-01-31
- **Evidence:** 8-K 20-Oct-2026 (Q3 2026): da Vinci procedures +~14%, Ion +~31%; FY2026 outlook: procedure growth ~14–15%, 'The Company expects to be closer to the midpoint of this range'; non-GAAP GM 68.7–69.3% (incl. ~0.9 pt tariff hit); opex growth 11–13%.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Management explicitly steers to ~14.5%; with Q3 at ~14% the outcome hinges on Q4 and on ISRG's rounding ('approximately 14%' would resolve NO). Slight lean below coin-flip because of the rounding convention.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Coin-flip on a midpoint the company itself points to (~50%).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if ISRG's reported FY2026 worldwide da Vinci procedure growth (Q4 2026 release or preliminary January announcement) is ≥14.5% as stated; 'approximately 14%' = NO, 'approximately 15%' or '14.5%' = YES.
- **Resolution source:** Intuitive Surgical Q4 2026 / preliminary FY2026 release (SEC EDGAR, CIK 1035267)
- **Sources used:** https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1035267/000103526726000067/q326ex-991earningsrelease.htm

His cost is recharged by CMI "on an actual-cost basis, without any mark-up" (+₹11 cr to the CMI RPT limit) `[PB-Nov26]`. The MD's pay therefore runs through the parent.
- **Other changes:** the CFO changed twice (Patil left Jan-2025; interim; Soma Ghosh from Jul-2025). Senior management person Pankaj Kapoor resigned Aug-2026 `[NSE filings]`.
- **Board:** 10 directors, 5 women; the chair (Jennifer Bush) and 3–4 non-executives are CMI nominees `[AR26]`. Non-executive CMI nominees take no pay. ID commission was approved by postal ballot (Oct-2026).
- **Incentives:** KMP remuneration ₹9.8 cr (FY25 ₹16.2 cr, which included transitions). CMI stock-based pay to CIL staff ₹14.4 cr "equity contribution" `[AR26 n.41]`. **Senior staff are paid in parent (US) stock, not CIL stock.** The incentive is aligned with CMI's global P&L, not with the CIL minority.
- **Tax and legal:** the Income Tax Department appealed to the Bombay HC on ₹210.77 cr of adjustments (nature not stated; likely transfer pricing, unverified) `[NSE 09-Jul-2026]`. GST demand of ₹5.19 cr plus an equal penalty (Jaipur, Oct-2026). Income-tax penalty of ₹0.95 cr (AY2018-19). All are small next to equity of ₹7,600 cr.

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-COST:hot-valuation-beats-spy-to-jun27`
- **Method:** valuation-temperature · **P(ours)** 0.42 · **P(base)** 0.48 · resolve by 2027-06-30
- **Evidence:** Yahoo monthly closes: COST $1,102.15 on 20-Nov-2026 — at its all-time high (52-wk $844–1,124) while SPY ($689.81) sits ~12% below its high. Q4 FY26 release (24-Sep-2026): FY26 net sales $297.2bn (+10.1%), comparable sales +8.4% (adjusted +6.6%), digital +20.9%; FY26 EPS $20.76 (Q4 $6.75 incl. a non-recurring $0.15 IEEPA tariff refund benefit) → ~53× trailing EPS.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Valuation-temperature test on a 'hot' quality compounder: ~53× earnings at an all-time high while the index is in a drawdown means a lot of defensive premium is already in the price; if markets recover, high-multiple defensives tend to lag. But quality compounders have repeatedly defied this, so we shade only moderately below the base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** A single US large cap beats SPY over ~7 months a bit under half the time (~48%; skewed single-stock returns).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if (COST close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 1,102.15) > (SPY close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 689.81). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits; special and regular dividends ignored.
- **Resolution source:** Yahoo Finance / Nasdaq closes (COST, SPY)
- **Sources used:** https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/COST; https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/SPY; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/909832/000090983226000084/costex9918-k92426.htm
- **Confidence of evidence:** verified

names) and its first-15 order.
**How it ran:** 25-Nov file → 404; the 24-Nov file holds DATE1 = 23-Nov-2026 on every row (byte-identical to the 23-Nov file) →
frame close **23-Nov-2026**. 1,547 symbols, all priced; **809** in band; 0 unmapped. In band: IT 38, FMCG 53, Consumer Durables 58;
no excluded subject present. **Eligible 149.**

allowed), but sector frames built on the NSE macro map carry commodity names; 53 FMCG names include sugar, tea, edible oil and
dairy mills.
